findings.explanation: The new GET /orders/<int:order_id> endpoint applies @require_auth (sets g.current_user) and then enforces ownership via is_owner_or_admin(g.current_user, order.user_id), returning 403 on failure. This exactly matches security-policy.md §3 ('Every endpoint that fetches an order by its identifier MUST verify ownership with is_owner_or_admin(current_user, order.user_id) before returning data') and api-spec.md ('/orders/<id> GET: owner or admin'). The helper is_owner_or_admin (app/auth.py:107-109) correctly returns user.id == owner_id or user.role == 'admin'. No IDOR or missing-authorization flaw is present.

evidence.content: A user may view ONLY their own orders. Every endpoint that fetches an order by its identifier MUST verify ownership with is_owner_or_admin(current_user, order.user_id) before returning data.
